zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價大跌，短端加入美債漲勢

油價大幅回落，緩解新一波能源衝擊的疑慮，美債週二全面上漲。2年期殖利率下跌7個基點至4.17%，10年與30年期各跌6個基點至4.64%與5.17%。週一漲勢偏向長端，這次對政策更敏感的短債也跟進。

伊朗與阿曼討論恢復荷姆茲海峽航運的臨時框架，布蘭特下跌6.69%至$86，WTI下跌4.65%至$81.06。另有報導指美國正準備讓外交官返回中東使館，降低全面衝突再起的疑慮。不過，10年期損益兩平通膨率仍為2.32%，名目殖利率降幅全數來自實質殖利率，後者也收在2.32%，並非中期通膨補償進一步縮小。

股票、信用基金與美債同步上漲，消費者信心雖轉弱，當前活動卻未同幅惡化。Collins與Barkin仍保留通膨改善不足時再升息的選項。利率市場之外，Kexim在紐西蘭取得資金，印度海外存款帶動本地買債，Braskem新重整架構則凸顯股東資金順位尚未解決。基準利率下降有利借款人，但各地資金供給及附帶條件仍有差別。

## 預期轉弱、當前數據有韌性，Fed維持利率仍有條件

Conference Board八月消費者信心指數下降0.8點至89.4，為年初以來最低，七月數字也遭下修。對企業景氣與勞動市場的預期降至一月以來最低，現況指標卻升至4個月高點。相較眼前情況，家庭更擔心未來。

其他資料並非全面疲弱。ADP每週就業增幅由9,500人提高至11,750人，Redbook銷售年增率由7.6%加速至9.1%。七月建築許可終值由137.4萬升至143.3萬，仍低於144.3萬的市場預期，月增4.3%也不及預期5%。六月S&P/Case-Shiller房價年增2.1%，高於前值1.6%與預期1.7%；另一項房價指數則在前月上漲0.3%後持平，年增率由修正後2.4%降至2.3%。

波士頓Fed總裁Susan Collins支持七月維持利率，目前也傾向繼續不動，但要求通膨朝2%進一步改善。她認為近期核心數字略為正面，月度波動卻使人難以確信趨勢；若進展無法持續，可能很快就有必要緊縮。Collins今年沒有投票權，預期先前關稅大部分已轉嫁，油價影響也將消退。不過，新供給衝擊或更強活動仍可能讓通膨偏高，AI建置對核心商品價格的壓力就是一例。

同樣無投票權的里奇蒙Fed總裁Tom Barkin表示，七月是否維持利率是相當接近的決定。等待可讓官員在9月15日至16日會議前，再取得兩個月資料。通膨持續下滑支持耐心，若價格壓力愈來愈根深蒂固，仍可能需要升息。週二油價大跌有利按兵不動，但每週消費、就業與Case-Shiller房價較強，也讓官員有理由保留升息選項。

Barkin另指出，只要投資人願意買，聯邦政府就能繼續借款；若這份意願消退，最終仍得面對調整。他未提出時間點，並以美元的全球地位及美國法治解釋需求為何持續。公共債務已超過$40兆，這項警告關乎長期融資能力，而不是預測眼前標售會失敗。

5年期美債殖利率下跌6個基點至4.35%。曲線變化不大，2年與10年期利差擴大1個基點至47個基點，2年與30年期擴大1個基點至100個基點。S&P 500上漲0.32%、Nasdaq 100漲0.64%、半導體漲1.44%，VIX下跌2.52%至15.45；LQD與HYG分別上漲0.64%及0.28%。利率下降支撐多種資產，並非資金由股票轉入債券避險。

## 回購預期使美債表現優於交換利率

財政部將長債回購至少加倍的訊號，不只影響名目殖利率，也反映在相對價格。公告後，美債表現優於同天期利率交換。30年期美債殖利率高於交換利率的差距，縮至二月以來最小；10年期差距縮小約3個基點至38個基點。這代表政府債相對變貴，不等於所有借款人的利率都同幅降低。

長債期貨選擇權也出現明顯偏多傾向，與較短天期不同。未平倉最集中的4個履約價中，九月及十二月買權未平倉量是賣權的兩倍以上。JPMorgan的8月24日調查顯示，回報做多與做空的投資人都增加，中性比率由67%降至54%。市場兩邊都在建倉，但官方可能加碼購債，已提高放空長債判斷錯誤的代價。

財政部可能動用現金，也加強了這種預期，因為回購時可不必立即發行等額國庫券抵銷。這仍是選項，並非已宣布決策。買權需求與回購推測已在影響部位，週二油價下跌則再提供買進久期的理由。

Stanley Druckenmiller質疑干預的前提。這位貝森特的前導師認為，支持債券價格會壓抑市場約束財政決策的訊號，而10年期殖利率接近名目經濟成長，並不算過度緊縮。即使相對價格改善，美債殖利率仍高於交換利率，10年期在4.6%以上，長債約5.2%。

國會同時考慮增加當年度$950億支出，主要與伊朗戰爭有關，卻沒有抵銷措施，另討論增加$3,500億國防支出。議員先前已放棄數千億美元的潛在刪減，年度撥款也可能延長至十二月中旬。貝森特財政提案或許包含減少詐欺，但先前政府效率改革未達成預期節省。調整買債時間，無法代替這些支出決定。

黃金上漲1.58%至$4,714，近1週漲幅接近8%、近1個月近16%，美元指數則下跌0.09%。實質殖利率下降有利無息資產，財政與政策不確定也提供避險理由，但不能把全部金價漲幅只歸因於對財政部的不信任。

## Kexim轉換融資幣別，印度存款創造本地買債需求

韓國進出口銀行Kexim發行NZ$6.25億、約$3.72億的5年期Kauri債，為約9年來首次進入紐西蘭境外發行人市場，也是韓國借款人在該市場的最大交易。這家AA級政策銀行原先指引至少NZ$2.5億，財務部門將選擇該市場的原因，直接連結至超大型雲端企業供給推高融資成本，以及投資人希望分散幣別。

紐西蘭今年債券發行約NZ$185億，甚至小於部分美國科技企業的單筆融資。Kexim已使用美元、歐元、澳幣、港幣及英鎊，如今找到科技債較少的市場。這筆交易顯示，核心市場擁擠會使非科技借款人轉往別處，即使小型市場無法承接整波AI融資。

Sycamore Tree Capital的Trey Parker更關心融資條件。Morgan Stanley與Moody's估計，未來AI資本支出達$3兆以上；JPMorgan將資料中心與電力納入後，預估逾$5兆。今年已發行的AI相關債務超過$4,000億。Parker擔憂的是到期時點、開發風險與私募結構評等，而不是直接把整個產業稱為泡沫。

美國保險監理官協會NAIC正在檢視，私募信貸評估是否充分區分評等及提供者。Parker指出，在尚未契約違約之前，評等認定改變就可能影響保險公司的監理待遇。他以2000年前後電信融資作比較，重點在時間落差：債市可以先資助產能，但商業需求還沒成熟，再融資期限就已到來。

資料中心借款人已向高收益投資人銷售部分投資級債務，承銷商也因需求轉弱而拉開交易間隔、放慢發行節奏。Parker偏好較短到期年限、信用強的租戶、較高本金攤還及額外收益補償。這些設計讓資本更早回收，降低對單一再融資時點的依賴。

印度方面，據知情人士表示，HSBC自七月以來至少買入$30億政府債，集中約5年期。截至7月30日，該行透過FCNR(B)海外存款計畫取得$63億，之後累計超過$100億。HSBC未回覆置評要求。印度央行優惠交換窗口避掉外幣風險，讓銀行取得可供投資的盧比。

全體銀行透過該計畫吸收的存款達$654億，體系剩餘流動性約₹4兆。自6月5日計畫開始，5年期政府債殖利率下降約31個基點，10年期則下降12個基點，新增資金對銀行主要買入天期的影響較大。

當地企業也規劃發債。Cholamandalam Investment and Finance可能發行₹200億、約$2.09億的永續債，10年後可贖回，規模可能追平印度金融業永續債紀錄，並創民營非銀行貸款人新高。公司六月當季貸款餘額年增22%。但若監理資本低於最低要求，該工具可以停止支付，發生損失後償還也需批准。Avenue Supermarts另計畫最多₹100億支應展店，為2019年以來首次、也是歷來最大發債。流動性充足，不代表永續資本工具等同一般優先融資。

## Braskem新資金順位未定，Aston Martin債權人尋求證據

約39%的Braskem債權人支持繼續協商$110億重整，使公司進入90天庭外程序。現在更尖銳的問題是股東資金排在哪裡。既有債權人希望其順位落後於自身債權，但架構僅記載這是他們的期待，並非有約束力的承諾。

持有Braskem約47%投票權的Petrobras，將原料貿易信用額度增加R$23.5億、約$4.56億，可維持營運並降低外部融資需求。股東認為供應商信用不能比照一般貸款，債券持有人則希望確保股東流動性不會排到自己前面。Petrobras抗拒債權人要求的直接增資，部分原因是可能必須合併Braskem財報，甚至在選舉年取得國會批准。

Braskem提議將到期延長5年，其中包括兩年半寬限期，並在尚未定義期限的紓困期內不減記本金。之後可能透過無投票權股票增資，但規模、時程與出資保證仍未確定。方案最終須取得超過半數受影響債權支持，才能獲法院批准；若失敗，可能轉入類似Chapter 11的司法程序。2030年美元債殖利率約22%，即使今年報酬達45%，石化利差改善仍未解決現金短缺。

Aston Martin債權人則就另一項順位爭議採取行動。Arini Capital Management與Tresidor Investment Management請求美國法院，向HPS、Authentic Brands、Moelis及Lazard發出傳票，取得文件與證詞，支持規劃中的英國訴訟。爭議涉及向BlackRock旗下HPS及英國Authentic Brands子公司籌措的£4.5億、約$6.13億，既有持有人認為交易繞過了他們。Aston Martin顧問Latham & Watkins則表示，交易符合相關法律及債券文件。取證請求只是尋找證據，並未判定哪一方解釋成立。

Delaware Life清理關係人曝險的過程，也使資產出售受到注意。公司承認分類錯誤後，將相關投資由約資產3%重列為逾40%、約$160億。Mark Walter同意出售湖人隊控制權，據報估值$125億；不到1年前取得時為$100億。TWG Global另計畫向Delaware Life購買最多$65億資產。

這些安排可能帶來現金或移轉曝險，卻未解決更廣泛的資本問題。保險公司、股東與借款人若彼此關聯，資產降評可能在出售價格轉弱時，同步提高法定資本要求。高價值球隊提供這個集團一項潛在資金來源，以不流動貸款為主的保險公司可能選擇較少。已宣布交易不等於現金已到位，也不能證明全部關係人風險都已移除。

## 主權買盤強，不代表每個公共部門資產負債表都改善

南非每週標售取得R147.9億投標，供給R25.5億，投標倍數5.8倍，為6月2日以來最強。2037年到期券供給R8.5億，吸引R67.1億投標，殖利率下降9個基點至8.75%。月底約R490億票息支應再投資，較強蘭特及通膨放緩也改善環境。

約翰尼斯堡的限制不同。Centre for Development and Enterprise指出，居民與企業欠市府的帳款，已由10年前R150億累積至R720億；人事費用達R207億，年度基礎設施投資卻降至最低R60億。市長Dada Morero在8月24日訪問中表示財務改善，市府上週也向Eskom支付R52.6億積欠電費。這筆款項處理了其中一項義務，但整體收款缺口仍壓迫公用事業與服務。

墨西哥對Pemex的支持，則把壓力移向主權。總統Claudia Sheinbaum兩年內安排逾$500億協助，前任期間另有約$800億。Pemex債務仍超過$700億，日產量低於170萬桶，約為20年前一半。支持降低了眼前違約風險，也使債務低於2018年高點，卻在預算赤字近乎倍增時增加政府融資壓力。

Moody's五月將墨西哥降至僅高於投機級一級，S&P也將其評等展望調為負向。國家是否繼續支持已較無疑問，更重要的是營運改革能否降低反覆援助的成本。更強的政府支持有利Pemex債權人，同時也消耗主權剩餘的信用緩衝。

## 接下來看通膨、航運與融資條款

8月26日七月PCE及8月28日Warsh的Jackson Hole演說，將檢驗週二漲勢的政策意涵。核心物價溫和、消費穩定，並清楚說明維持利率的條件，有助鞏固2年期殖利率降幅；通膨偏強或再升息條件仍不明，則使這波回落較脆弱。

伊朗與阿曼討論也需要轉為實際荷姆茲船流，以及較低的運費與保險成本。再度中斷、美國施壓中國購買伊朗原油，或更廣泛的報復關稅循環，都可能逆轉供給改善。週二10年期損益兩平通膨率維持2.32%，若之後與短端殖利率一起上升，就不同於當日實質殖利率下降的有利組合。

信用市場資金仍在，但保障條件正持續協商。新AI融資的保證與攤還安排、Braskem股東資金順位，以及Aston Martin取證程序，將釐清現金流不如預期時由誰承擔損失。這些條款的重要性，遠超過發行首日的訂單規模。

overall_summary.session_narrative:

消費者預期轉弱，現況、每週就業及零售資料卻較有韌性。Collins與Barkin傾向等待，但要求通膨持續改善。回購預期影響部位，美債相對交換利率也轉強。

Kexim轉往紐西蘭避開擁擠市場，印度存款則支持HSBC買債。Braskem取得39%支持後進入協商，卻未保證新資金順位落後。Aston Martin債權人尋求證據，保險與公共部門案例也顯示融資風險最終落點。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Cheaper oil brings the front end into the Treasury rally

Treasuries rallied across the curve on Tuesday as a sharp oil decline eased fears of another energy shock. Two-year yields fell 7 basis points to 4.17%, while 10- and 30-year yields dropped 6 basis points to 4.64% and 5.17%. Monday's gains had been concentrated in longer maturities; this time policy-sensitive debt participated as well.

Brent fell 6.69% to $86 and WTI lost 4.65% to $81.06 as Iran and Oman discussed an interim framework to restore Strait of Hormuz shipping. Reports that the US was preparing to return diplomats to Middle East embassies also reduced fears of renewed full-scale conflict. Ten-year breakevens nevertheless held at 2.32%. The nominal yield decline came entirely through real yields, which also closed at 2.32%, rather than a further reduction in medium-term inflation compensation.

Equities and credit funds gained alongside Treasuries, while consumer confidence weakened without a matching collapse in current activity. Collins and Barkin still left another Fed hike available if inflation failed to improve. Away from the rates rally, Kexim found funding in New Zealand, Indian diaspora deposits supported local bond purchases, and Braskem's new restructuring framework exposed an unresolved dispute over shareholder-credit priority. Easier benchmarks were helping borrowers, but the supply of money and the terms attached to it differed considerably.

## Weaker expectations meet resilient current data and a conditional Fed hold

The Conference Board's August confidence index fell 0.8 point to 89.4, its lowest since the start of the year, after a downward revision to July. Expectations for business conditions and the labor market weakened to their lowest since January, while the present-conditions measure reached a four-month high. Households were less confident about what comes next than about current circumstances.

Other data were mixed rather than uniformly weak. Weekly ADP employment growth improved to 11,750 from 9,500, and Redbook sales growth accelerated to 9.1% from 7.6% a year earlier. Final July building permits rose to 1.433 million from 1.374 million but missed the 1.443 million consensus; the 4.3% monthly gain also fell short of the expected 5%. June's S&P/Case-Shiller house-price measure rose 2.1% from a year earlier, up from 1.6% and above the 1.7% consensus. The separate house-price index was flat on the month after a 0.3% gain, with annual growth easing to 2.3% from a revised 2.4%.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins continued to favor holding rates after supporting July's decision, but required further progress toward 2% inflation. Recent underlying readings were mildly encouraging, she said, with monthly volatility limiting confidence. If improvement did not persist, tightening could be warranted soon. Collins, a nonvoter this year, expected much of the earlier tariff pass-through to have occurred and the oil-price effect to wane. She also warned that new supply shocks or stronger activity could keep inflation high, including pressure on core goods from the AI build-out.

Richmond's Tom Barkin, also a nonvoter, called the July hold a close decision. Waiting would provide two more months of data before the September 15–16 meeting. Declining inflation would support patience, while evidence that price pressure was becoming embedded could still require a hike. Tuesday's oil drop helped the hold case, but the firmer weekly spending, jobs and Case-Shiller figures gave officials reasons to keep that option open.

Barkin separately said federal borrowing could continue while investors remained willing to buy, but warned of an eventual reckoning if that willingness faded. He set no date and cited the dollar's global role and US rule of law as reasons demand persisted. With public debt above $40 trillion, the warning concerned longer-term financing capacity, not an imminent failed auction.

Five-year Treasury yields fell 6 basis points to 4.35%. The curve changed little: 2s10s widened 1 basis point to 47 and 2s30s widened 1 to 100. The S&P 500 rose 0.32%, Nasdaq 100 gained 0.64%, semiconductors advanced 1.44%, and VIX fell 2.52% to 15.45. LQD gained 0.64% and HYG 0.28%. Lower rates supported broad asset returns without a flight from equities into bonds.

## Buyback expectations help Treasuries outperform swaps

Treasury's signal to at least double long-bond purchases was visible in relative pricing as well as outright yields. Treasuries had outperformed equivalent-maturity swaps since the announcement. The excess of 30-year Treasury yields over swap rates narrowed to its smallest since February; at 10 years, the gap shrank about 3 basis points to roughly 38. That describes government bonds becoming relatively richer, not a comparable reduction in every borrower's interest rate.

Long-bond futures options also developed a pronounced bullish skew, unlike shorter sectors. Across the four most populated strikes, September and December call open interest was more than twice the put total. JPMorgan's August 24 survey found more investors reporting both long and short positions, while neutral responses fell to 54% from 67%. Investors were taking positions on both sides, but the possibility of more official purchases had increased the cost of being wrong on a long-bond short.

Possible use of Treasury cash added to that expectation because it could fund purchases without immediately issuing offsetting bills. It remained an option rather than an announced decision. Tuesday's oil move supplied a separate reason to buy duration, against a backdrop already shaped by call demand and buyback speculation.

Stanley Druckenmiller challenged the intervention's premise. Bessent's former mentor argued that support for bond prices suppresses the signal through which markets discipline fiscal policy. He did not consider a 10-year yield around nominal economic growth unduly restrictive. Treasury yields still exceeded swaps, with the 10-year above 4.6% and the long bond near 5.2%, despite the relative improvement.

Congress, meanwhile, had considered $95 billion of additional current-year spending, largely for the Iran war, without offsets, and discussed another $350 billion of defense outlays. Lawmakers had abandoned hundreds of billions in prospective cuts, and annual appropriations were likely to be extended into mid-December. Fraud reduction could feature in Bessent's fiscal proposal, but earlier government-efficiency efforts had not delivered the expected savings. A change in purchase timing does not settle those spending decisions.

Gold rose 1.58% to $4,714, almost 8% higher over a week and nearly 16% over a month, while the dollar index eased 0.09%. Falling real yields supported a non-interest-bearing asset; fiscal and policy uncertainty offered additional reasons to retain protection. The gold move cannot be attributed solely to distrust of Treasury policy.

## Kexim changes currencies; Indian deposits create local bond demand

The Export-Import Bank of Korea sold NZ$625 million, or $372 million, of five-year Kauri notes, its first issue in that offshore New Zealand market in about nine years and the largest by a Korean borrower. The AA-rated policy bank had initially indicated at least NZ$250 million. Its treasury department linked the choice to higher funding costs caused by hyperscaler supply and investors' desire for currency diversification.

New Zealand issuance this year totals about NZ$18.5 billion, less than some individual US technology financings. Kexim, which had already used dollars, euros, Australian dollars, Hong Kong dollars and sterling, found a market with little technology debt. The deal shows how crowded core markets can redirect a non-technology borrower's funding, even though a smaller venue cannot absorb the entire AI wave.

Sycamore Tree Capital's Trey Parker focused on the terms behind that wave. Morgan Stanley and Moody's estimate coming AI capex of $3 trillion or more, while JPMorgan projects over $5 trillion including data centers and power. More than $400 billion of AI-linked debt has already been sold this year. Parker's concerns were maturity timing, development risk and ratings of private structures, rather than a blanket description of the sector as a bubble.

The National Association of Insurance Commissioners is examining whether private-credit assessments adequately distinguish among ratings and providers. Parker described the risk that an insurer's regulatory treatment could change with a rating designation before any contractual default. His comparison with telecom finance around 2000 concerned timing: debt markets can fund capacity before commercial demand is ready, bringing refinancing due before expected cash flows arrive.

Data-center borrowers have approached high-yield investors even for IG-rated debt, and underwriters have spaced transactions and slowed calendars in response to weaker demand. Parker favors shorter maturities, strong tenants, substantial amortization and extra compensation. Those features return more capital earlier and reduce dependence on a single refinancing date.

In India, HSBC has bought at least $3 billion of government bonds since July, concentrated around five years, according to people familiar with the purchases. It raised $6.3 billion through the FCNR(B) diaspora-deposit program by July 30 and subsequently took its total above $10 billion. HSBC did not respond to a request for comment. The RBI's concessional swap window hedges the foreign-currency exposure and leaves banks with rupees to invest.

System-wide deposits under the scheme reached $65.4 billion, and surplus banking liquidity rose to about ₹4 trillion. Five-year government yields have fallen about 31 basis points since the program began on June 5, compared with 12 for the 10-year. The additional cash has therefore had a larger effect around the maturities banks are buying.

Local companies are also planning supply. Cholamandalam Investment and Finance could issue ₹20 billion, or $209 million, of perpetual bonds callable after 10 years, potentially matching the largest perpetual sale by an Indian financier and setting a private nonbank record. Its loan book grew 22% year on year in the June quarter. Payments on the instrument can stop if regulatory capital falls below the minimum, and repayment after losses requires approval. Avenue Supermarts separately plans up to ₹10 billion for store investment, its first bond since 2019 and largest yet. Ample liquidity does not make a perpetual capital claim equivalent to ordinary senior funding.

## Braskem's new money has no settled priority; Aston Martin creditors seek evidence

About 39% of Braskem's creditors backed continued negotiations on its $11 billion restructuring, moving the company into a 90-day out-of-court process. The sharper issue is now what shareholder funding would rank behind. Existing creditors want it subordinated to their claims, but the framework records that as their expectation, not a binding promise.

Petrobras, which owns about 47% of Braskem's voting capital, increased its raw-material trade-credit limit by R$2.35 billion, or $456 million. That can keep operations running and reduce outside funding needs. Shareholders argue supplier credit should not be treated as a conventional loan; bondholders want firm protection against shareholder liquidity ranking ahead of them. Petrobras has resisted the direct equity commitment sought by creditors, partly because consolidation and possible congressional approval could follow in an election year.

Braskem proposed five-year maturity extensions, including a two-and-a-half-year grace period, and no haircut during an undefined relief period. Fresh equity could subsequently come through nonvoting shares, but its size, timing and backstop remain open. A plan ultimately needs support from more than half of affected claims for court approval; failure could lead to a judicial process resembling Chapter 11. Its 2030 dollar notes yielded about 22% despite a 45% return this year. Better petrochemical spreads had improved bond performance without resolving the cash shortage.

Aston Martin creditors pursued a separate priority dispute. Arini Capital Management and Tresidor Investment Management asked a US court to subpoena HPS, Authentic Brands, Moelis and Lazard for documents and testimony supporting a planned UK challenge. They contest £450 million, or $613 million, raised from BlackRock's HPS and a UK Authentic Brands subsidiary, arguing that the transaction circumvented existing bondholders. Aston Martin adviser Latham & Watkins says it complies with law and bond documents. A discovery request seeks evidence; it does not decide which interpretation prevails.

Delaware Life's effort to unwind affiliated exposure brought asset sales into focus. It restated such investments from about 3% of assets to more than 40%, or roughly $16 billion, after acknowledging classification errors. Mark Walter agreed to sell control of the Lakers at a reported $12.5 billion valuation after acquiring it for $10 billion less than a year earlier. TWG Global also plans to buy up to $6.5 billion of assets from Delaware Life.

Those arrangements may provide cash or move exposure, but they do not settle the wider capital question. When an insurer, its owner and borrowers are connected, an asset downgrade can increase statutory capital requirements while sale prices are weakening. A valuable sports franchise offers one possible source of funds for this group; an insurer holding mainly illiquid loans may have fewer choices. The announced transactions should not be treated as completed cash proceeds or proof that all affiliated risk has been removed.

## Strong sovereign demand does not reach every public balance sheet

South Africa's weekly auction received R14.79 billion of bids against R2.55 billion offered, a 5.8 bid-to-cover ratio and the strongest demand since June 2. The 2037 bond drew R6.71 billion for R850 million offered, with its yield falling 9 basis points to 8.75%. About R49 billion of month-end coupons supported reinvestment, alongside a firmer rand and moderating inflation.

Johannesburg faces a different constraint. Bills owed to the city have accumulated to R72 billion from R15 billion a decade ago, according to the Centre for Development and Enterprise. Employee costs reached R20.7 billion while annual infrastructure investment fell as low as R6 billion. Mayor Dada Morero said in an August 24 interview that finances were improving; the city paid Eskom R5.26 billion in overdue power bills last week. That payment addressed one obligation, while the broader collection shortfall continues to pressure utilities and services.

Mexico's support for Pemex has shifted pressure toward the sovereign. President Claudia Sheinbaum arranged more than $50 billion of assistance in two years, following roughly $80 billion under her predecessor. Pemex debt remains above $70 billion and production below 1.7 million barrels a day, about half its level two decades ago. Support has reduced immediate default risk and debt from its 2018 peak, but added to government financing pressure as the budget deficit nearly doubled.

Moody's cut Mexico to one notch above speculative grade in May, and S&P placed a negative outlook on its rating. Continued state support is less in question than whether operational reform can reduce its recurring cost. A stronger claim on government backing helps Pemex creditors while drawing on the sovereign's remaining credit cushion.

## Inflation, shipping and financing terms are the next checks

July PCE on August 26 and Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole speech will test the policy interpretation of Tuesday's rally. Subdued underlying prices, steady consumption and a clear explanation of the conditions for holding would reinforce the lower 2-year yield. Firmer inflation or continued uncertainty about another hike would leave that relief more vulnerable.

The Iran-Oman discussions also need to produce actual Hormuz traffic and lower freight and insurance costs. Renewed disruption, US pressure on Chinese purchases of Iranian oil or a broader retaliatory tariff cycle could reverse the supply relief. Ten-year breakevens stayed at 2.32% on Tuesday; a simultaneous rise in them and the front end would be a less favorable development than the day's fall in real yields.

In credit, liquidity is available but its protections are being negotiated. New AI guarantees and amortization schedules, Braskem's shareholder-money priority and Aston Martin's discovery process will clarify who bears losses if cash flows disappoint. Those terms will matter well beyond the first day's order book.
